Subject: Orion Health Partners — availability rider proposal + MSA/SOW attachment routing

James —

Thanks for the productive discussion last week. Per our call with procurement and engineering, attached is a first-pass availability rider and a short telemetry/evidence annex for the order form and MSA/SOW attachments. High-level summary of what we included: 

- Availability commitment: 99.95% monthly uptime for API-serving endpoints (measured over the service region specified in the order form).
- Latency target: 95th percentile API response time under 300ms for interactive traffic (see annex for measurement windows and sampling methodology).
- Grace for scheduled maintenance: up to 3 hours/month (standard maintenance window); will be excluded from availability calculations if communicated 72 hours in advance.
- Evidence & telemetry: we will provide 90 days of aggregated telemetry exports, live uptime dashboards, and rolling 30/90-day incident summaries. SOC 2 and audit report references included in the annex.
- Credits & exceptions: tiered service credit schedule included. We also included a narrow exception carve for long-running batch jobs and planned major upgrades (per Section 4).

Attachments (stubs):
- 20261108_orionhp_availability_rider_draft.pdf (draft rider)
- 20261108_orderform_redlines.docx (order form markups)
- telemetry-evidence-annex_v1.pdf (telemetry definitions + evidence path)

Ask: please review the rider and annex and let us know whether the uptime/latency commitments and the evidence path are acceptable to Orion procurement and security. If OK, we can prepare an order-form-ready annex and route for signature via DocuSign.

Proposed next steps:
1) Procurement confirms acceptance (or sends prioritized redlines) by COB Nov 12.
2) We incorporate redlines and provide an order-form-ready PDF for signature.
3) Execute via DocuSign and onboard SSO/KMS keys in the following sprint.

If helpful, Grace and Karthik are looped for any technical clarifications or evidence mapping.

Thanks,

Markus Klein

Markus —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear draft. A few questions/requests from procurement and our security team: 

1) Credits schedule: can you provide the exact credit percentages per downtime band (example: <99.95%, 99.5-99.95, <99.5) and capping rules for maximum monthly credit? Procurement wants the table in the order form (we need to show finance).

2) Evidence retention: security asked whether 90 days of telemetry is the minimum or if you can extend to 180 days for a limited subset (uptime & incident timelines) — if there is a cost implication, please flag it.

3) SOC 2 / audit: please confirm the most recent SOC 2 type II report period and whether we can request a read-only evidence pull for specific incidents during our contract term.

4) We noted Section 4 carveouts for batch jobs — can you add a clear definition of what qualifies as a "batch workload"? We need that text to be tight to avoid future disputes.

Procurement contact for routing and counterparty review is procurement@orionhp.com (cc'd). Happy to hop on a 30-min call if that helps.

Thanks,

Markus / Karthik —

Looping back after reviewing James' notes. My read and suggested approach:

- Credits table: accept providing a simple, explicit table in the order form. Proposed default:
  - Monthly uptime >= 99.95%: no credit
  - 99.9% <= uptime < 99.95%: 10% service credit (of monthly service fees)
  - 99.0% <= uptime < 99.9%: 30% service credit
  - uptime < 99.0%: 100% credit up to one month cap
  (These numbers are negotiable, but they give procurement a clear finance-facing view.)

- Retention: agree to provide 90 days by default; offer a 180-day retention package as a paid add-on for the metrics subset (uptime events + incident timelines). We should call out pricing impact in the order form appendix.

- SOC 2: confirm latest SOC 2 Type II is Q2 2026 (report attached in vendor pack). We can allow a read-only evidence pull under NDA for incident investigations; will need a request workflow and SLO to respond.

- Batch workload definition: suggest wording — "Batch workload: non-interactive requests processed asynchronously, where individual request latency is not measured against interactive SLOs; examples include bulk-embedding jobs, model training checkpoints, long-running export jobs exceeding 60s per single API call."

- Maintenance windows: keep 3 hours/month as-is; propose that scheduled maintenance with 72-hour notice is excluded; unscheduled emergency maintenance must be logged with incident notes.

I attached a quick set of redlines for the order form (orderform-redlines.docx) with the credits table and the batch definition inserted. Also note that Finance will ask for the credit cap language (we should be explicit that credits do not exceed 100% of monthly fees).

If you want, I can draft the brief email back to James with the tightened language and the pricing note.

Grace O'Connor
Senior Contracts Manager | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com
